correctness.rationale: Every factor either contains the unique 10 or avoids it. The second class is only unary or 0^i1^j; explicit occurrence counts and shorter-prefix/suffix tests exhaust all cases and produce exactly the five families. A standard-library program independently checks 2,401 quadruples and 95 joint coefficients, but the all-parameter proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: An exact four-run binary MUS factor classification, its bivariate word-length/count generating function, and the sharp length-specific maximum were not present in the inspected generic sliding-window MUS and run-length-encoding literature. The strongest nearby exact prior theorem gives a 2r-1 generic bound (seven at four runs), whereas five is the new sharp binary bound; the generic unary-run lemma covers only a portion. Mathematical comparison is substantive and non-exhaustive, with clear residual risk of an unlocated specialization.
residual_risks: The generic RLE algorithms can instantiate this family; an existing source may have already specialized them symbolically without appearing in indexed searches.
No broad cross-database uniqueness conclusion is justified; exact novelty awaits independent literature review.

value.rationale: Minimal unique substrings underpin unique-substring queries. Four binary runs are the first alternating pattern with two 01 occurrences and a unique 10 boundary. The exact five-family phase diagram, sharp maximum five (versus the general RLE upper bound seven), all-length bivariate distribution, first extremal length eight, and asymptotic dominance of extremizers form a complete natural classification, not a handpicked finite table. The claim makes no unproved general-algorithm improvement.
